summary: Iteration-3 backend regression for the two reported bugs is FULLY VERIFIED. 6/6 tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter3_bugfixes.py. FIX 1 (wrong-character lip-sync) verified: POST /projects/{id}/episodes/1/scenes/1/lines/scene-1-line-1/shot returned QUEUED with a fresh prediction_id, DB shows a closeup_clips record whose character_id=CHARACTER_A (the SPEAKING character of that line) and a lipsync_clips record with stage='CLOSEUP'; polling drove CLOSEUP -> LIPSYNC -> READY with a valid video_url (both stages observed via DB during polling). FIX 2 (dialogue re-render) verified: after the line reached READY, a second POST returned QUEUED + a NEW prediction_id (not the old READY short-circuit), a fresh closeup_clips entry was created, and the lipsync stage was reset to CLOSEUP; no video_url was returned on the start response. FIX 2b (motion re-render) verified: POST /scenes/1/motion on a scene whose master motion was already READY returned QUEUED with a NEW prediction_id different from the previously stored READY prediction_id (video_clips row updated to QUEUED). FIX 3 (voice change applies on re-render) verified: changed CHARACTER_A voice from Bill -> Ellen via /characters/{cid}/voice, then the FIX-2 re-render for the same line re-synthesized the audio_assets take — voice_id now equals the newly-assigned voice (BIvP0GN1cAtSRTxNHnWS) instead of the initial Bill voice. Cost control was strictly respected: exactly ONE close-up->lipsync polled to READY, ONE extra dialogue-shot start (not polled), ONE motion re-render start (not polled), and one ElevenLabs re-synth. Existing series 8e3af3cb50604f03a3911154b80d166b (already had script + character images + storyboards + one READY master motion) was reused; it was undeleted (previous iteration soft-deleted it via test teardown) so no new assets were generated. One transient Cloudflare 502 was observed on the FIX-2b POST during the first run and immediately succeeded on retry (edge-side hiccup, not backend).

minor.issue: One transient Cloudflare 502 (Ray a3cc9e559992c365) observed on first attempt. Backend logs show no error; likely edge hiccup. Retry succeeded. Non-blocking, but the frontend should already treat non-JSON 5xx from the edge as retryable (already handled by api.ts JSON.parse guard).

action_items: No code changes required — the three fixes (single-character close-up sourcing, re-render short-circuit only on QUEUED/PROCESSING, and voice re-synth on take mismatch) are behaving exactly per the spec.

Optional hardening: the dialogue-shot POST leaves the previous READY close-up/lipsync artifacts orphaned in Emergent Object Storage when a re-render replaces the entry. Consider a background cleanup of the old storage_paths when the entry is overwritten, otherwise storage grows unbounded per re-render.

Optional UX: expose the CLOSEUP-vs-LIPSYNC stage in the serialize_episode line.shot payload (currently only status/error/video_url are exposed) so the frontend can show 'Rendering close-up...' vs 'Lip-syncing...' — the info exists on lipsync_clips[].stage but isn't projected.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.start_dialogue_shot correctly guards short-circuit only on ('QUEUED','PROCESSING') and always re-runs start_luma_closeup for READY/FAILED — this is the exact fix for FIX 2.
routes.start_dialogue_shot re-synthesizes audio only when voice_id or text differ from the existing audio_asset — cheap, idempotent, and correctly triggers on voice change (FIX 3).

routes.start_dialogue_shot uses _asset(ep, 'character_reference', character_id=line['character_id']) to source the close-up frame — this is what guarantees the correct-character face is animated (FIX 1). Regression test test_fix1_start_dialogue_shot_uses_speaking_character_closeup asserts DB.closeup_clips[].character_id == line.character_id.

poll_dialogue_shot correctly transitions stage CLOSEUP -> LIPSYNC by starting PixVerse against the archived close-up video (not against the multi-character master motion clip) — this was the root cause of the reported wrong-character animation and is now correct.
routes.start_motion short-circuit also correctly narrowed to ('QUEUED','PROCESSING') — FIX 2b.
Minor concern: on re-render, the previous READY close-up/lipsync/audio storage paths in Emergent Object Storage are orphaned (no delete). Not a correctness bug, but storage will grow per re-render.

rca_of_issue: Reported bugs — RCA and fix verification: (1) 'Wrong character lip-syncing' — root cause: previous pipeline applied PixVerse lip-sync directly to the scene MASTER motion clip which can contain multiple characters, so PixVerse animated whatever face was at frame-center rather than the speaker. Fix: start_dialogue_shot now first renders a single-character speaking close-up via Luma seeded from _asset('character_reference', character_id=line.character_id) (SPEAKING character's own reference image, per buildy build_dialogue_closeup_prompt), records it in a new closeup_clips list, and poll_dialogue_shot transitions stage CLOSEUP -> LIPSYNC by feeding THAT close-up (not the master) into PixVerse. Verification: closeup_clips[scene=1,line=scene-1-line-1].character_id == CHARACTER_A (== manifest speaker), lipsync_clips[...].stage == 'CLOSEUP' at start, shot reaches READY through both stages. (2) 'Re-render not working' — root cause: start_dialogue_shot and start_motion previously short-circuited whenever the existing clip.status was READY, so a re-render POST just returned the old artifact. Fix: both now short-circuit only when status is in {'QUEUED','PROCESSING'}, allowing READY/FAILED to be re-rendered. Verification: after the line reached READY, a second POST returned status=QUEUED with a NEW prediction_id (proof: closeup_clips entry replaced with the new prediction_id, lipsync stage reset to CLOSEUP); analogous behaviour verified for /motion. (3) 'Voice change not applying' — root cause: audio was cached and never re-synthesized. Fix: start_dialogue_shot re-runs synthesize_voice whenever audio_asset.voice_id != current locked voice or audio_asset.text != line.text. Verification: after switching CHARACTER_A voice from Bill to Ellen and re-rendering the line, audio_assets[line=scene-1-line-1].voice_id == 'BIvP0GN1cAtSRTxNHnWS' (Ellen), not the initial 'pqHfZKP75CvOlQylNhV4' (Bill).
